chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: Breakdowns and pushing a Cadillac to Dennison
summary: Booking agents scheduled long jumps and the band had to make the job to be paid; they pushed one broken Cadillac with another to Dennison.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Just considering life on the road -- because I know the Blue Devils did more traveling than almost any other band. They were always on the road. They did endless one-nighters.
Yeah, mmm-hmm.
What was life like doing that...?
Tough.
Describe it. What was the worst thing about it?
Well, the thing was that the booking agents got to booking the jobs so far apart...
Business-wise.
Yeah. In other words, there was such long jumps. And the car would fall apart. They'd break down on you and cause you to miss the job.
You mean you wouldn't get paid.
No.
You had to make the job to get paid.
Yes!
Does this mean you'd have to sleep in the cars?
Oh, we did it many times. Sleep in the car...
Did you have cars or a bus?
Buster Smith - 39

No, we had mostly cars all the time. During them days, a bus cost so much more money, that the band wasn't making enough money to buy a bus, and we couldn't rent because it cost too much. So we'd buy old ugly(?) cars and try to fix them up and make the jobs.
How many cars did you have? Two...
Two and three. You had to have two. I'll never forget that we had two old Cadillacs, they were old-timey Cadillacs with the top down...
You mean like a drop-head?
Yeah. And we got out here in Abilene, Texas, and one of throwed the rod...
Did what?

Throw the rod(?) in the motor. And it locked the motor, and we didn't have time to get it fixed. And the man told us that it took him two days to fix it. So we just took the other old Cadillac and got behind it and shoved it all the way clean through Dallas here, and rode up there to Dennison, Texas, and played the gig, and when we got through playing that night, we got behind it and shoved it all the way back to Dallas here.
You mean you were towing it. You towed the other car.
Yeah, pushing it.
Pushing it.
Yes!
Buster Smith - 40
Not physically.
Yeah. All the boys sitting in the car, and driving the other one behind, pushing it. ....(?)...., the car was ruined.
I want to understand this. You had two cars. You've got one that can only go in neutral.
Right.
And you've got the other car behind it, and you pushed the first car with the second car.

Yeah. Ho-ho-ho. We did that. We didn't have time to get it fixed, so we had to go up and make the dates, and we had two free days off here, and we had the man to fix it up in Dallas. So we just shoved all the way over to (?), 200 some odd miles, and come on through here and on up to Dennison.
